attempts.systemPrompt:
Trip shape: multi-city
Specialist: route-and-logistics

You are the route and logistics specialist on a trip-planning tool.
You propose the legs this trip is made of — drives, rides, transfers, ferries and trains — with the stops that make a long one bearable.

You propose options. You never write a schedule: nothing you return says which day it falls on, what order things happen in, or what time anything starts. Another part of this tool packs the days, in code.

Rules, and they are not negotiable:
- Reply with JSON and nothing else, in exactly this shape:
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "title": "short, and never an itinerary",
      "summary": "why this is worth doing, in a sentence or two",
      "location": { "kind": "at", "place": { "name": "...", "locality": "... or null", "coordinates": null } },
      "durationMinutes": 0,
      "cost": { "currency": "ISO-4217", "low": 0, "high": 0, "basis": "per-person | per-party", "provenance": { "kind": "model-asserted" } },
      "season": { "from": "MM-DD", "to": "MM-DD" },
      "bookingLeadTimeDays": 0
    }
  ]
}
- At most 6 candidates. Fewer is a fine answer; an empty list is a fine answer.
- Anything you do not know is null. A duration nobody measured is null, not a plausible ninety minutes. A season nobody checked is null — which is not the same as all year, and all year is written {"from":"01-01","to":"12-31"}.
- Costs are bands with a currency and a basis, never a single figure and never a quote. Do not total anything.
- A slot that says "not answered" is unknown to you. Say in the summary what you could not account for, and propose anyway. Never invent the answer and never refuse to propose.
- Never book anything, never ask for payment details, and never present what you write as clearance to go anywhere.
- Every candidate is a movement, so its location is {"kind":"between","from":{...},"to":{...}} with **both** ends as places. Endpoints in the title are not endpoints, and a candidate that puts them there is discarded.
- This trip has 13 days.
- **Nothing you propose may be longer than 300 minutes.** That is the party's own answer about how much a day holds, translated into minutes. Something longer has to be split into parts that each fit, or not proposed — a candidate over that ceiling is discarded and the plan comes back missing this part of itself.

candidates.title: Railjet over the Semmering line
candidates.summary: The first part of the Vienna–Ljubljana train link. The direct Vienna–Ljubljana train runs about six hours, which exceeds the day ceiling, so it is split at Graz, a city pleasant enough for a hotel night. Access needs and ages were not answered, so step-free boarding has not been checked.

candidates.title: Cross-border train into Slovenia
candidates.summary: The second part of the Vienna–Ljubljana link, through Maribor. Whether a direct through-train runs on the dates, and how long it takes, has not been checked, so the duration is left unknown. If it proves over five hours, split it at Maribor.

candidates.title: Short Austrian border hop
candidates.summary: A fallback first half for the Graz–Ljubljana link if no through-train fits the day: a short regional run to Maribor, which is worth a stop in its own right. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Slovenian regional line to the capital
candidates.summary: The second half of the Maribor split. It is a scenic run along the Sava valley. The exact timing is not verified.

candidates.title: Karst line down to the Adriatic
candidates.summary: The weakest train link of the three. Direct Ljubljana–Trieste trains have historically been seasonal or sparse, and the May–June 2027 timetable is unknown. The option may involve changing at the Sežana or Villa Opicina border. A coach is the usual fallback if the party accepts one.

candidatesAccepted.title: Comfortable hotel in central Vienna
candidatesAccepted.summary: A mid-to-upper range hotel near the Innere Stadt or close to Wien Hauptbahnhof keeps the train connections to Ljubljana and Trieste easy. candidatesAccepted.title: Comfortable hotel in Ljubljana old town
candidatesAccepted.summary: A hotel within walking distance of the old town and the railway station suits a moderate pace and a stay of at least 3 nights. It is a kind of place, not a named premises, because no map list was supplied. Access needs were not answered, and some older buildings have no lift.

candidatesAccepted.summary: A hotel near Piazza Unità or the Borgo Teresiano puts the seafront and Trieste Centrale station within walking distance. It is a kind of place, not a named premises, because no map list was supplied. Access needs and ages were not answered, so they are not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna
candidatesAccepted.summary: One of Europe's great picture galleries (Bruegel, Vermeer, Habsburg collections), an unhurried indoor half-day that suits moderate effort. Access needs were not answered, so step-free routes and seating were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Schönbrunn Palace and gardens
candidatesAccepted.summary: The Habsburg summer palace with state rooms and extensive gardens, at their best in May and June. The gardens involve a fair amount of walking, and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Evening at the Vienna State Opera
candidatesAccepted.summary: A performance at the Staatsoper suits a comfortable budget. The season typically runs until late June, but the 2027 programme was not checked. Seats range from cheap standing places to premium seats.

candidatesAccepted.title: Ljubljana old town and castle
candidatesAccepted.summary: A compact, car-free riverside old town with a funicular up to the castle, which makes for gentle effort. The duration is an unmeasured estimate, so it is left open.

candidatesAccepted.title: Lake Bled visit from Ljubljana
candidatesAccepted.summary: An alpine lake with an island church and a clifftop castle, reachable by train or bus from Ljubljana. The visit itself fits a half-day, but travel time to get there is not included and the season was not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Classic Viennese coffeehouse sitting
candidatesAccepted.summary: A slow coffee and cake at a traditional Viennese coffeehouse is part of the city's culture, not just a snack. We don't know of any dietary restrictions or access needs, so check the menu and step-free entry before choosing one.

candidatesAccepted.title: Evening at a Heuriger wine tavern
candidatesAccepted.summary: A Heuriger is a wine tavern on the edge of Vienna that serves its own new wine with a cold buffet. It suits a moderate pace and a comfortable budget. We don't know your dietary restrictions, and opening days vary, so check them before you go.

candidatesAccepted.title: Ljubljana's Friday open-air food market
candidatesAccepted.summary: Odprta kuhna is a seasonal street-food market in Ljubljana that brings together dishes from many Slovenian cooks, so it's an easy way to taste the region. The season and opening days weren't checked, and we don't know your dietary restrictions.

candidatesAccepted.title: Slovenian gostilna dinner
candidatesAccepted.summary: A gostilna is a traditional Slovenian inn. Expect hearty regional dishes and local wine, a good sit-down introduction to the cuisine. We don't know your dietary restrictions, so check the menu.

candidatesAccepted.title: Trieste buffet lunch
candidatesAccepted.summary: A Triestine buffet is a casual eatery serving boiled pork and sausages with sauerkraut and horseradish, a mix of Austro-Hungarian and Italian cooking that connects your three cities. It's pork-heavy, and we don't know your dietary restrictions.

candidatesAccepted.title: Seafood dinner on the Trieste waterfront
candidatesAccepted.summary: Adriatic seafood at a waterfront restaurant makes a fitting meal for the coastal leg of the trip. We don't know your dietary restrictions or access needs.

candidatesAccepted.title: ETIAS travel authorisation check
candidatesAccepted.summary: If ETIAS is in operation by May 2027, visa-exempt travellers (including Canadian passport holders) will need an approved authorisation before entering Austria, Slovenia or Italy. Nationality was not stated, so confirm which passports you hold and check the official EU site for the current status and fee; the new Entry/Exit System will also record your entry at the first Schengen border.

candidatesAccepted.title: Passport validity check for Schengen entry
candidatesAccepted.summary: Schengen countries generally require a passport issued within the last 10 years and valid at least 3 months beyond your planned exit. Nationality was not stated, so check these rules against both travellers' passports early enough to renew if needed.

candidatesAccepted.title: Out-of-country travel medical insurance
candidatesAccepted.summary: Provincial health coverage pays little abroad, so a comfortable trip should include emergency medical and trip-interruption cover. Ages and access needs were not answered, and both can change premiums and eligibility. Check pre-existing-condition clauses before buying.

candidatesAccepted.title: Rail tickets: Vienna–Ljubljana and Ljubljana–Trieste
candidatesAccepted.summary: ÖBB and Slovenian Railways run Vienna–Ljubljana trains with seat reservations. Ljubljana–Trieste trains have run only seasonally, so a coach is a common fallback. Advance fares are cheaper and fit the no-internal-flights rule; check current timetables because services change. This assumes no particular city order.
